title: Object Pronouns with Gerundio and Infinitivo
description: Master pronoun placement and attachment rules with non-finite verb forms.

vocabulary.source: I'm going to buy it for him/her
I'm going to buy it for him/her
can you pass it to me?
he/she is telling it all to me
I don't know how to tell it to him/her

grammar.title: Object Pronouns with Gerundio and Infinitivo
grammar.content:
At B2, you need to master the placement of clitic pronouns (me, te, lo, la, le, nos, os, los, las, les, se) when combined with non-finite verb forms — gerundio and infinitivo.

With conjugated verbs, pronouns go BEFORE the verb: 'Lo veo.'
With gerundio and infinitivo, pronouns can go in TWO positions:

1. **Attached to the end** (most common in speech):
   - Gerundio: 'estoy haciéndolo' / 'haciéndomelo'
   - Infinitivo: 'voy a hacerlo' / 'voy a dárselos'

2. **Before the conjugated auxiliary**:
   - Gerundio: 'lo estoy haciendo'
   - Infinitivo: 'lo voy a hacer' (also: 'voy a hacerlo')

⚠️ DOUBLE PRONOUN RULE: When there are TWO pronouns (OD + OI) with a gerundio or infinitivo:
- They can BOTH attach to the end: 'dándomelo'
- OR both go before the conjugated verb: 'me lo está dando'
- They CANNOT be split!

⚠️ ACCENT RULE: When attaching pronouns to gerundio or infinitivo, check if the accent needs to be added:
- 'hablando' + 'lo' → 'hablándolo' (accent to maintain stress on 'lan')
- 'hacer' + 'lo' → 'hacerlo' (no accent needed — stress already on 'ce')
- 'estudio' + 'lo' → 'estudiándolo' (accent needed)

⚠️ LE/LI → SE change: When le/les is combined with lo/la/los/las, 'le' becomes 'se': 'se lo di', NOT 'le lo di'.

rows: Se lo di (NOT le lo di)

examples: Lo estoy buscando por toda la casa. (I'm looking for it all over the house.)
Voy a comprárselo a mi madre. / Se lo voy a comprar. (I'm going to buy it for my mother.)
¿Me lo puedes pasar, por favor? (Can you pass it to me, please?)
Está contándomelo todo. (He/She is telling it all to me.)
No sé cómo decírselo. (I don't know how to tell it to him/her.)
¡Deja de llamarme así! (Stop calling me that!)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian also has clitic pronouns (îl, o, îi, le, mă, te, ne, vă) but the attachment rules are different — Romanian pronouns almost always come BEFORE the verb. Spanish attachment is a unique feature. The LE→SE change has no direct Romanian parallel since Romanian doesn't have the same le/lo distinction.

pronunciation.title: Stress in Attached Pronouns
pronunciation.content:
When pronouns are attached to gerundio or infinitivo, the stress pattern changes. An accent mark is often needed to maintain the original stress:

GERUNDIO + PRONOUNS:
- hablando + lo → hablándolo (ha-BLAN-do-lo) — accent on 'lan' to maintain stress
- comiendo + lo → comiéndolo (ko-MYE-n-do-lo) — accent on 'ie'
- yendo + lo → yéndolo (YEN-do-lo) — accent on 'ye'
- contándomelo (con-TÁN-do-me-lo) — accent on 'tan'

INFINITIVO + PRONOUNS:
- hacer + lo → hacerlo (ah-SEH-loh) — NO accent (stress on 'ce' already correct)
- dar + lo → dárselo (DAR-seh-loh) — accent on 'dar' to maintain stress
- decir + te + lo → decírtelo (de-SEER-teh-loh) — accent on 'ci'
- entregar + se + la → entregársela (en-tre-GAR-seh-la) — accent on 'gar'

RULE: If the natural stress after attaching pronouns is on a different syllable than before, add an accent mark to restore it.
pronunciation.aid_note: Romanian pronouns never attach to infinitives — they always precede the verb: 'să-l fac' (to do it) vs Spanish 'hacerlo'. The accent mark rules in Spanish are more complex due to the fused form.

exercises.question: Where do object pronouns go with a conjugated verb?
options: At the end of the sentence
They don't go with conjugated verbs
exercises.explanation: Object pronouns go BEFORE the conjugated verb: 'Lo veo' (I see it).

exercises.question: What happens when 'le' or 'les' is combined with 'lo/la/los/las'?
exercises.explanation: When 'le/les' is combined with 'lo/la/los/las', 'le' changes to 'se': 'se lo di' (I gave it to him), NOT 'le lo di'.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Voy a ____ (buy) el regalo para mi madre. → Voy a ____.' (I'm going to buy the gift for my mother.)
exercises.explanation: 'Comprárselo' — pronouns attach to the infinitive: le + lo → se lo + comprar → comprárselo. An accent is needed to maintain stress.

exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
exercises.explanation: Both are correct! Pronouns can go before the conjugated verb ('Lo estoy leyendo') or attached to the gerundio ('Estoy leyéndolo'). Both mean the same thing.

exercises.question: Complete: '¿Me ____ (you) ____ (pass) el libro, por favor?' (Can you pass me the book, please?)
exercises.explanation: '¿Me lo puedes pasar, por favor?' — pronouns go before the conjugated verb: me lo + puedes pasar. Or attached: ¿Puedes pasármelo, por favor?

exercises.question: What is 'deja de llamarme así' in English?
exercises.explanation: 'Deja de llamarme así' = 'Stop calling me that!' — Imperative + 'de' + infinitive + attached pronoun 'me'. The pronoun is attached to 'llamar'.
